body.x: Polyn Technology announced it will present a live demonstration of its NeuroVoice Voice Activity Detection (VAD) chip at CES 2026, showcasing what the company describes as the first practical application of its silicon-proven Neuromorphic Analog Signal Processing (NASP™) technology. The demonstration will run from January 6 to 9 at Hall G, Booth 61701 at the Venetian Expo.

The live demo features Polyn’s first NASP chip performing always-on voice detection with microwatt-level power consumption and microsecond-scale latency. By performing neural network inference directly in the analog domain rather than in digital form, the chip enables continuous, reliable speech detection while drastically reducing energy consumption. This capability addresses a longstanding challenge for battery-powered and always-listening devices, where power efficiency is critical.

body.cap: Aleksandr Timofeev, CEO of Polyn Technology. | Photo by Polyn Technology

body.x: “This CES demo shows how the NASP technology platform moves from validation to practical functionality,” said Aleksandr Timofeev, CEO of Polyn Technology. “Voice detection is a highly sought-after feature, but only if it can run continuously without draining power. That’s exactly what analog neuromorphic processing enables.”

According to the company, the VAD core represents the first milestone in Polyn’s broader voice-processing roadmap. Additional NASP-based cores, including speaker recognition and voice extraction, are currently under development. These technologies are intended for deployment across consumer electronics, critical communications equipment, robotics, and industrial systems. Polyn positions its next-generation VAD capabilities as a foundation for “voice-to-intent” systems, enabling physical AI, mission-critical voice applications, privacy-focused wearables, and autonomous machines through always-on, ultra-low-power edge intelligence.

body.cap: NeuroVoice VAD Chip on Demo Board | Photo by Polyn Technology

body.x: During CES 2026, Polyn will also provide information on NeuroVoice evaluation kits and early-access programs aimed at companies developing ultra-low-power, voice-controlled products. In addition, the company plans to share its product roadmap for NASP-based solutions targeting automotive, critical communications, and other applications, with availability scheduled for 2026.

Polyn Technology is a fabless semiconductor company specializing in neuromorphic analog signal processing, focused on bringing AI capabilities to the sensor edge with unprecedented energy efficiency. The company operates offices across the UK, Israel, the United States, Europe, and Asia.
